Armani.known: Milanese ease; Acqua di Giò, twice Fragrance of the Year
Armani.about:
Giorgio Armani started his house in Milan in 1975 with his partner Sergio Galeotti, bankrolled by the sale of his Volkswagen Beetle. The fragrances arrived in 1982, and in 1996 Alberto Morillas composed Acqua di Giò, inspired by the sea and sky around the island of Pantelleria. It took Men's Fragrance of the Year twice, entered the Fragrance Hall of Fame in 2012, and at one point made up about 30% of everything Armani sold in perfume. Armani Code (2004) followed, its bottle shaped after a tuxedo's satin lapels.
I Will (2026) is the house's first new men's pillar in two decades: four years and 2,800 trials by Morillas and Nathalie Lorson, with Madagascar vanilla stripped of its usual sweetness and set over a woody-leather base.

Claude Marsal.about:
Claude Marsal is a young house, launched in 2016 and sold through the Perfumes 4U family of boutiques across Canada and the US. It keeps a low profile: no founder's biography, no credited perfumer, so we describe the juice rather than a legend. The idea is music, blending notes the way a composer builds a harmony, with every scent named for a melody, an instrument or a piece, from La Mélodie to Le Piano to Le Concerto.
What we carry is the warm end of the line. La Mélodie Maximal opens on mandarin, grapefruit and sea notes before oakmoss, guaiac wood and a pour of whisky; Le Piano and Or Noir Café are the two we kept reaching for. Rich, long-lasting and easy to recommend.

Ferragamo.known: Shoemaker to the stars; black-tie Florentine scents
Ferragamo.about:
Salvatore Ferragamo spent the 1920s in Hollywood making shoes for Mary Pickford, Gloria Swanson and Joan Crawford, then came home to Florence in 1927 and opened the workshop that became the house. The modern fragrances began in 1998 with pour Femme by Jacques Cavallier; pour Homme followed a year later and won Men's Fragrance of the Year at the 2000 FiFi Awards. Signorina (2012) added a panna cotta accord and a cap tied with the house's Vara bow.
Uomo Signature (2018) is Alberto Morillas's black-tie version of Uomo: mandarin and pink pepper over cardamom and cinnamon, then roasted coffee, leather and tonka. The matte-black bottle stands for the house's tuxedos.

Gabriella Antosh.known: Zoltan: icy mint into cinnamon and leather
Gabriella Antosh.about:
Gabriella Antosh is a sister label to Claude Marsal, from the same North American retail group, and it launched in 2018 with Zoltan for him and Gizella for her. No perfumer is credited and the brand publishes no history, so the fragrance has to speak for itself. Zoltán, for what it's worth, is a Hungarian name that traces back to the word sultan.
Zoltan opens cold, with grapefruit, mint and blood mandarin, then turns on rose, cinnamon bark and blond leather over tonka and patchouli within the hour. The label has since gone women-only and Zoltan has dropped out of its lineup, which is part of why we keep it.

Givenchy.known: Parisian couture; the Audrey Hepburn legacy
Givenchy.about:
Hubert de Givenchy opened his couture house in Paris in 1952 and met Audrey Hepburn the next year, fitting her for Sabrina. In 1954 he had perfumer Francis Fabron make a scent for her alone, and for three years nobody else could buy it. When he said he would sell it, she reportedly answered "Mais je vous l'interdis!" (but I forbid you), and L'Interdit (1957) became the house's first fragrance, with Hepburn widely cited as the first star to front a perfume campaign.
Gentleman arrived in 1974, built by Paul Léger on patchouli. Gentleman Réserve Privée (2022), by Nathalie Lorson and Olivier Cresp, is its after-dark edition: a whisky accord made from Scottish distillery barley, chestnut and iris over cedar and vetiver.

Jean Paul Gaultier.about:
Jean Paul Gaultier launched his label in 1982 and his first perfume in 1993: a corseted torso in a tin can that some shops refused to stock ("they found it scandalous, the can"). It won Women's Fragrance of the Year and was renamed Classique. Its counterpart, Le Male (1995), was composed by a 26-year-old Francis Kurkdjian around the smell of a 1950s barbershop and poured into a sailor's torso in Gaultier's striped marinière. He thought the packaging would never work; it entered the Fragrance Hall of Fame in 2011 and is still called one of the world's three best-selling men's fragrances.
Le Male Elixir (2023), by Quentin Bisch, is the darkest take yet: lavender and mint over honey, vanilla, benzoin and tobacco, at parfum strength.

Maison Francis Kurkdjian.known: A perfumer's own house; Baccarat Rouge 540
Maison Francis Kurkdjian.about:
Francis Kurkdjian wrote Le Male at 26, opened the first bespoke-perfume atelier in 2001 and recreated Marie Antoinette's perfume for Versailles before founding his own house in Paris in 2009 with Marc Chaya, a dinner-party acquaintance who had asked him what he did. ("I am a perfumer.") Since 2021 he also directs perfume creation at Dior.
Baccarat Rouge 540 began as a commission for the crystal house's 250th anniversary: 250 crystal bottles at €3,000 each in 2014, named for the 540 °C at which gold-dusted crystal turns Baccarat red. It joined the regular line in 2015, sold out its six-month supply in a month, and is now one of the best-selling fragrances in the world. Petit Matin (2016) is its opposite number, Paris at dawn: lemon and lavandin over orange blossom and musk, made as a pair with Grand Soir.

Maison Margiela.known: Replica: a memory, a place and a year on every label
Maison Margiela.about:
Martin Margiela founded his house in Paris in 1988 and became fashion's Greta Garbo: no interviews, press answered by fax and signed "we", staff in white lab coats, blank white labels held by four stitches. Replica, the fragrance line, takes its name from his 1994 collection of faithfully reproduced vintage clothes. Each bottle wears a cotton label like the clothing tags, printed with a memory, a place and a year.
The first three (2012) came from Jacques Cavallier and Marie Salamagne; Flower Market's "Paris 2011" was Cavallier's own summer walk. Jazz Club (2013), by Aliénor Massenet, was the line's first for him: Brooklyn, 2013, rum, tobacco leaf and vanilla. Coffee Break (2019) is Cavallier again, coffee and milk mousse under lavender. In 2025 Replica's Afternoon Delight won Fragrance of the Year.

Nishane.known: Istanbul's first niche house; extraits with a story
Nishane.about:
Mert Güzel and Murat Katran met at a friend's birthday party in 2010 and discovered they shared the same dream: Istanbul's first niche perfume house. They founded Nishane (Turkish for "sign" or "mark") in 2012, self-funded, and took sixteen extraits to Milan's Esxence fair in 2015. Jorge Lee composed the early signatures, among them Wūlóng Chá, Suède et Safran, Fan Your Flames (after Rumi: "Seek those who fan your flames") and Hacivat (2017), named for a character of Ottoman shadow theatre. Cécile Zarokian's Ani (2019) honours a ruined city on the Turkish-Armenian border and a folk song three nations claim.
The founders are credited as co-noses, and every collection carries a story: the Esperanto-named Time Capsule (Kredo, belief; Tempfluo, the flow of time; Papilefiko, the butterfly effect; Tero, earth; Deziro, desire) by Jean-Louis Sieuzac, Anne Flipo, Dominique Ropion, Carlos Benaïm and Alberto Morillas, and the X Collection, the tenth-anniversary reworkings of its biggest hits. Still independent, still run by its founders.

Parfums de Marly.known: The perfumed court of Louis XV; a star perfumer per launch
Parfums de Marly.about:
Julien Sprecher founded Parfums de Marly in Paris in 2009 and named it for the Château de Marly, Louis XV's retreat from Versailles and the heart of what became known as the perfumed court. The château is gone; the Horses of Marly that Guillaume Coustou carved for it stand in the Louvre, and they ride on every bottle with the date 1743. The scents are named for horses and horsemen, and each launch goes to a different star perfumer.
Pegasus (2011) was the first big hit, Hamid Merati-Kashani's Layton (2016) the breakthrough, and Quentin Bisch's Delina (2017) the bestseller. Althaïr (2023), by Merati-Kashani and Ilias Ermenidis, is a Bourbon vanilla the house traces to the vanilla first brought to France under Louis XV; Kalan (2019) sets lavender and orange blossom, the formal French garden, over pepper and woods.

Tom Ford.known: Black Orchid, Private Blend and a FiFi for Noir
Tom Ford.about:
Tom Ford left Gucci and founded his own house in April 2005. His first fragrance, Black Orchid (2006), began with a flower: he had growers hunt down one of the darkest orchids in existence, "deep, dark chocolate" rather than true black, and David Apel built the scent around it with black truffle and vanilla. Private Blend followed in March 2007, twelve scents launched at once, Tuscan Leather and Tobacco Vanille among them, and it made Tom Ford a name in niche.
Noir (2012), by Olivier Gillotin, won Men's Fragrance of the Year at the 2013 FiFi Awards; Oud Minérale (2017) and Noir Extreme Parfum (2023) took the luxury category. Noir Extreme (2015) and Ombré Leather (2018) are both Sonia Constant's; Café Rose (2012, relaunched 2023) is Antoine Lie's. The house style has never changed: heavy concentration, dark woods, leather and tobacco in black-and-gold glass.

Valentino.about:
Valentino Garavani opened his house on Rome's Via Condotti in 1960, and that July met Giancarlo Giammetti, an architecture student who gave him a lift home in his Fiat and became his partner in everything. The first fragrance came in 1978. Olivier Polge's Valentino Uomo (2014) put roasted coffee and a hazelnut-chocolate gianduja cream into a men's scent.
Born in Roma (2019), with the house's Rockstud studs on the bottle, is Antoine Maisondieu and Guillaume Flavigny's Rome: mineral salt, violet leaf and smoked vetiver. The flankers take the city at different hours, Yellow Dream (2021), Coral Fantasy (2022), Green Stravaganza (2024) and Purple Melancholia (2026), and in 2024 the Uomo Intense took the Fragrance Foundation's Consumer Choice award. The brand says Born in Roma now ranks among the top three prestige fragrances in the US.

Versace.about:
Gianni Versace opened his first boutique on Milan's Via della Spiga in 1978 and released his first fragrance three years later. The Medusa came in 1993, from the mosaic floors of the Roman ruins in Reggio Calabria where he and his siblings played as children; whoever loves Medusa, he said, has no way back. Alberto Morillas has shaped much of the house's scent, from Bright Crystal (2006) to Dylan Blue (2016).
Eros (2012), by Aurélien Guichard, is named for the god of love and bottled in turquoise glass meant to look like the Mediterranean: mint and green apple over tonka, vanilla and ambroxan. Eros Najim (2024), by Jordi Fernández, takes the Arabic word for star and heads for the desert at sunset: saffron, caramel, oud and frankincense, launched first in the Middle East.

Xerjoff.known: Perfume as art; stone flacons and meteorites
Xerjoff.about:
Sergio Momo, a Turin designer and former children's-book illustrator, took his nickname, Joff, from his Slavic grandmother; London colleagues made it Sir Joff, and Xerjoff was born. He made two perfumes in quartz flacons, a buyer at a Moscow design fair asked for thirty, and the company was registered, officially in 2007. The idea was perfume as an art object: rare materials in hand-polished stone and glass with gold caps. Xerjoff revived Casamorati, a Bologna perfumery whose trademark dates to 1888, and its Shooting Stars scents ship with a certified fragment of the meteorite that fell on Siberia in 1947.
Erba Pura (2013) and Erba Gold (2016) are both by Chris Maurice: Sicilian citrus and fruit over musk, amber and vanilla, with ginger and cinnamon in Gold. Alexandria II (2012) and Naxos (2015) are the other names fans know. Soprano began in 2018 under Xerjoff's Sospiro label and now lives in the Vibe collection: lychee and Bulgarian rose over a milky accord, with oud, patchouli and leather beneath.

Yves Saint Laurent.about:
Yves Saint Laurent took over at Dior at 21, then founded his own house with Pierre Bergé in 1961; Y, the first fragrance, followed in 1964. Opium (1977), by Jean Amic and Jean-Louis Sieuzac, launched in New York aboard a tall ship with Truman Capote at the helm, caused a scandal over its name and sold $30 million in Europe in a year; it won Women's Fragrance of the Year in 1979. Kouros (1981) and Paris (1983) followed it to the FiFi stage.
La Nuit de L'Homme (2009), by Anne Flipo, Pierre Wargnye and Dominique Ropion, the team behind L'Homme, is cardamom and lavender over cedar and tonka, the after-dark edition. Y (2017) and MYSLF (2023) are the house's latest Men's Fragrance of the Year winners.

Hermès.known: In-house perfumers; mineral woods, no musk
Hermès.about:
Hermès began in 1837 as Thierry Hermès's harness workshop in Paris, and perfume came more than a century later. Its first, Eau d'Hermès (1951), was Edmond Roudnitska's answer to a brief about the inside of an Hermès bag where a perfume had lingered. 24 Faubourg is in the Fragrance Hall of Fame. Since 2004 the house has kept its perfumer in-house: Jean-Claude Ellena, who never wears perfume himself, and since 2016 Christine Nagel.
Ellena's Terre d'Hermès (2006) was built from mineral and vegetable notes only, no musk and no animal notes, around a flint accord; it won Men's Fragrance of the Year on both sides of the Atlantic in 2007. For the Eau de Parfum Intense (2025) Nagel wanted lava stone, found there was no such extract, and built one, then added roasted coffee and liquorice wood.

Dior.known: Miss Dior, Roudnitska's Hedione, iris for men
Dior.about:
On February 12, 1947, Christian Dior showed his first collection, the New Look, and filled the salon with his first fragrance, Miss Dior, by Paul Vacher and Jean Carles. The name came from his sister Catherine, a Resistance fighter who survived Ravensbrück: when she walked in during the naming, a friend called out, "Voilà Miss Dior!" Edmond Roudnitska then gave the house Diorissimo (1956), built around lily of the valley, Dior's lucky flower, and Eau Sauvage (1966), the first fragrance to use Hedione, a jasmine molecule that changed modern perfumery. Poison and J'adore are in the Fragrance Hall of Fame; Sauvage, Men's Fragrance of the Year in 2016, is widely reported as the world's best-selling men's scent.
Olivier Polge's Dior Homme (2005) put iris at the heart of a men's fragrance, and Dior Homme Intense (2007) turned it up. Since 2021 the perfumes have been led by Francis Kurkdjian.

Sospiro.known: Xerjoff's sister house, tuned to opera
Sospiro.about:
Sospiro is Xerjoff's sister house, created by the same Turin designer, Sergio Momo, two decades into his career. Xerjoff, named for Momo's childhood nickname Joff, built its reputation on perfume as an art object: rare materials in hand-polished stone flacons, a revived 1888 Bologna perfumery (Casamorati) and scents shipped with fragments of a Siberian meteorite. In 2011 Momo opened a second door to the same workshop and called it Sospiro, Italian for a sigh, the moment beauty catches in your chest. Where Xerjoff looks to art and rare stone, Sospiro looks to the opera house: its fragrances carry musical names like Accento, Capriccio, Duetto, Opera Grande and Bel Canto.
The two houses share perfumers and ideas. Erba Pura, now one of Xerjoff's best-known scents, was born at Sospiro in 2013 and moved across six years later. Erba Leather, by Christian Provenzano, is the Erba line's suede side: passion fruit, bergamot and lemon over leather, jasmine and sandalwood, with amber and vetiver underneath.

Louis Vuitton.known: Flat-top travel trunks since 1858; perfume since 1927; master perfumer Jacques Cavallier Belletrud
Louis Vuitton.about:
In the spring of 1835, a 13-year-old named Louis Vuitton left his village in the Jura mountains and set out for Paris on foot. It was roughly 470 kilometres, he paid his way with odd jobs, and he arrived two years later. In Paris he apprenticed with a trunk maker and packer, and he became so good at it that Empress Eugénie trusted him to pack her wardrobe. In 1854 he opened his own workshop, and four years later he broke the rules: a flat-topped canvas trunk, when almost every trunk was rounded leather. Flat trunks could be stacked in a train car or a ship's hold, and travellers never forgot his name. Travel has been the house's story ever since.
Perfume is part of that story too, and it started earlier than most people realise: Heures d'Absence in 1927, Je, Tu, Il in 1928 and Eau de Voyage in 1946. The formulas are lost; only the bottles survive.
In 2012 the house brought in Jacques Cavallier Belletrud, born in Grasse to a family that has lived there since the fifteenth century, with a father and grandfather who were perfumers before him. He had already written L'Eau d'Issey for Issey Miyake. He restored Les Fontaines Parfumées, a perfumery in Grasse, as the house's own workshop, and in 2016, after a seventy-year silence, Louis Vuitton was making perfume again. He composes every one himself, and many of them are about the feeling of arriving somewhere new. Imagination (2021), five years in the making, is that feeling bottled for the road.

Dolce & Gabbana.known: Sicilian glamour; Light Blue and The One
Dolce & Gabbana.about:
Domenico Dolce, born in 1958 in Polizzi Generosa, a hill town in Sicily, and Stefano Gabbana, born in Milan in 1962, met in 1982 while working for the same Milan fashion house; Dolce had phoned to ask about a job. They opened a design studio together the next year, showed their first women's collection in the New Talents section of Milan Fashion Week in 1985, and staged their first show of their own, Donne Vere (Real Women), in 1986. Sicily never left the clothes: black lace, the 1988 collection Il Gattopardo, named after Visconti's film The Leopard, and Alta Moda shows staged in Taormina. The first perfumes, Dolce&Gabbana Pour Homme and Pour Femme, came in 1990, and Pour Femme was named best feminine fragrance of 1993 by the Perfume Academy. Since 2022 an in-house company, Dolce&Gabbana Beauty, has run the fragrances.
The One launched for women in 2006 and for men in 2008. Olivier Polge's 2015 Eau de Parfum is the denser take on the men's: grapefruit and basil over ginger and cardamom, settling into tobacco, amber and cedar.
